name: Fairmont Peace Hotel
positioning: Historic Bund hotel in Shanghai, formerly the Cathay Hotel, with views of Pudong across the Huangpu River
best_for: Travelers who want a historic hotel on the Bund
Guests who enjoy live jazz and hotel heritage

facts.text: The hotel is on the Bund with views of Pudong across the Huangpu River.
The Peace Museum traces the legacy of the former Cathay Hotel, the predecessor of Fairmont Peace Hotel, from 1929 to the present day.
Hotel guests are invited to a complimentary 30-minute guided tour of the Peace Museum.
The Sassoon Presidential Suite occupies the entire 10th floor penthouse, where the hotel's creator and former owner, Victor Sassoon, once lived.
The hotel has a series of country-themed suites, including a Japanese Suite with tatami mats and shoji screens.
The Cathay Room on the 9th floor was formerly Sir Sassoon's private banquet hall and has a 270-degree riverfront terrace.
Dragon Phoenix is on the 8th floor and has dragon-phoenix ceiling motifs and red pillars with views of the Bund and Lujiazui.
The Jazz Bar hosts nightly performances by the Old Jazz Band, which holds a Guinness World Record.
Fairmont Gold guests have access to a ninth-floor lounge with private check-in, complimentary breakfast and all-day refreshments.
An indoor pool is on level one, part of the Willow Stream Spa on the same floor.
The front door of the hotel opens onto Nanjing Street, and the rooms are well soundproofed.
Indoor parking is included, with 20 parking spaces.

highlights.text: The Jazz Bar has nightly performances by the Old Jazz Band, a Guinness World Record holder.
The Cathay Room, once Sir Sassoon's private banquet hall, has a 270-degree riverfront terrace.
The Sassoon Presidential Suite fills the 10th floor penthouse where Victor Sassoon once lived.
The Peace Museum traces the legacy of the former Cathay Hotel, with a complimentary guided tour for guests.
Country-themed suites include a Japanese Suite with tatami mats and shoji screens.

considerations.text: Condé Nast Traveler says this is not a family-focused hotel, and the hushed interiors are not ideal for young children.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects its luxury positioning and prime Bund location.
WhataHotel notes the historic building may have smaller rooms than modern hotels.
